phrases.text: Measure CS asks the voters of this school district whether to approve $77 million in school bonds.
The district would sell the bonds and repay them from a yearly tax on property in the district.
Measure CS needs 55 percent of the vote to pass.
The bond money could pay only for the school projects the measure lists.
Those include repairing classrooms, heating, air conditioning, plumbing and electrical systems, improving safety and security, and replacing leaky roofs.
The district's tax rate statement estimates a tax of $31.96 per $100,000 of assessed value each year, through 2056-2057.
The statement estimates the total to repay, with interest, at about $153.7 million.
Supporters say Measure CS would fund safety and repair work at every school without raising the current school bond tax rate.
Opponents say district enrollment is falling, and that taxes would drop when the old bond ends unless Measure CS extends them.
A yes vote approves the $77 million in school bonds.
A no vote rejects the $77 million in school bonds.
